If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimation.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–3% in late horizon (16–30 days) to correct for momentum reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for early horizon to capture bullish momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for mid horizon to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >2% from true path, apply a 1.0–1.5% correction in late horizon to dampen volatility.
